info.title: Keyup
info.description:
Searchable archive of the radio traffic an [sdrtrunk](https://github.com/dsheirer/sdrtrunk)
recorder captures: every call, its metadata, its transcript, and the tools to find, play,
correlate and export it.

* **Reading needs no account.** Everything that *changes* data needs a session
  (`POST /api/auth/login`) or an API token (`Authorization: Bearer kup_…`); a cookie-authenticated
  mutation must also send `X-Requested-With: keyup`.
* **One filter set.** The parameters of `GET /api/calls` work identically on `/calls/facets`,
  `/calls/export`, `/calls/playlist.m3u`, `/search`, `/stats/*`, `/timeline` and the live feed.
  Array filters repeat (`?talkgroup=1101&talkgroup=1102`).
* **Patch-aware.** A patch is a temporary supergroup of talkgroups; every call stores *all*
  the talkgroups it involved, so `talkgroup=1101` finds patched traffic carrying 1101 too.
* **Two clocks, always.** Every call carries `started_at` (ISO 8601 UTC) and `started_local`
  (naive local time, the `TZ` setting), because the recorder, the dispatchers and any CAD system all think
  in local time. Time-of-day and day-of-week filters work on the local clock.
* **Pagination.** `page`/`page_size` (≤ 500) for tables, or `cursor=` keyset paging for long
  scrolls, which cannot skip or repeat a row while new calls arrive. A paged list also returns
  the matching row count, in `total` and in the **`X-Total-Count`** header — capped at 50 000,
  where `total_capped` becomes true. A cursor page returns `total: null`: an infinite scroll
  shows no total, and counting for one meant a full scan of the filtered set per page.
* **Audio** is served from `GET /api/calls/{id}/audio` with HTTP `Range`, a strong `ETag`
  (the file's sha256) and a long private `Cache-Control`; `GET /api/calls/{id}/waveform` gives
  a cached peak envelope for a player.
* **Links** (`/api/links`) tie a call or a conversation to a record in another system — a CAD
  incident, a case number — and outbound webhooks tell that system when calls and links change
  (docs/WEBHOOKS.md).
* **Live**: `WS /api/live` (send a filter object as the first frame) or `GET /api/live/sse`.

post.description: Exchanges a username and password for the `keyup_session` cookie (HttpOnly, SameSite=Lax). The cookie alone is not enough to change data: every mutation must also carry `X-Requested-With: keyup` and a same-site `Origin`. Five failures per username or address in fifteen minutes are answered with 429.
Deletes the session row and clears the cookie. Safe to call when already signed out.

get.description: Answers 200 for anonymous callers too, with `user: null` — the SPA uses it to decide whether to show the editing controls. `auth_required_read` reports whether reading this deployment needs an account at all.

Filtered, paginated list of recorded transmissions. Accepts the whole common filter set (see the parameters below — the same set works on `/calls/facets`, `/calls/export`, `/search` and the live feed) and both pagination styles: `page`/`page_size`, or `cursor` for a stable infinite scroll. `total` is counted only for `page`/`page_size` — it is null while cursor paging — and stops at 50 000, where `total_capped` becomes true. It is also returned in the `X-Total-Count` header whenever it was counted.

post.description: One observation window for one site: the live control channel, the secondary control channels it advertises, the band plan, the traffic channels granted, the neighbors announced and the control frequencies the recorder is configured to hunt. The document is stored verbatim and folded into the site's channel inventory, where repeated windows accumulate counts rather than replacing each other. `instance` — the recorder's own `instance_id` — is stored beside the window, so a site two boxes both hear can be read one box at a time (`GET /api/sites/{site_id}/message-mix?instance=…`). post.summary: Post a batch of radio events
post.description:
Up to 1 000 control-channel events about subscribers — unit registration and de-registration, group affiliation and affiliation queries, location registration, SNDCP grants and pages, and the ack/deny/queued responses to all of them. Needs a Bearer token with the `upload` scope, the same one `/api/call-upload` and `/api/recorder/observations` use. The batch's `instance` — the recorder's own `instance_id` — is stamped on every row it stores, and is what `GET /api/radios/{radio_id}/events?instance=…` filters on.

The batch is **idempotent** on `(site, at, kind, opcode, radio_id, talkgroup)`: a recorder that spooled a batch through a network failure may resend it, and the resend costs nothing — note that the key does *not* include `instance`, so when two recorders hear one message the row keeps whichever instance arrived first. A `kind` the archive does not know is stored as `other` with the opcode kept, and **one bad event never costs the batch** — the response counts `stored`, `duplicates` and `rejected` instead.

Icecast has no dry run — a mount either accepts a source or it does not — so this is the only honest check of the Server, Port, Mount, Username and Password from the feed's *Feed Technical Details (Advanced)* panel. No call audio is published. It does briefly occupy the mount, so it fails while another broadcasting client holds it, which is usually the answer being looked for. Checks as much of a service's configuration as can be checked **without publishing a call**, and says in `checked` exactly what that was. Broadcastify Calls is tested with the documented `test=1` parameter alongside `apiKey` and `systemId` — a real check of the credentials that registers no call and returns no upload URL — against whichever endpoint `broadcastify_environment` selects, with the credentials belonging to that same environment. OpenMHz has no such check: its public `/{shortName}/calls` read resolves the short name, but its API key is only ever validated by a real upload. The Broadcastify result also carries the host clock offset (`clock_offset_s`, `clock_ok`, `clock_source`), which is step 1 of their upload workflow. Nothing is uploaded here and no switch is changed.

An `uploaded` row is refused: that row **is** the guarantee the call was not published twice, and re-sending it would publish it twice. The second question is the one that matters, because a server can answer `/health` and still not have the model loaded. Nothing is written: this does not touch the worker's router, the queue or any call. The probe runs synchronously and is capped at 45 seconds, and at most two run at once across the API process — a third gets `429`, because a probe occupies a web worker for as long as it takes. A backend whose engine runs in-process (`faster_whisper_local`, `openvino_genai`) is health-checked — which for those means the model loads — but **not** benchmarked: transcribing here would contend with the transcription worker for the same device and time a path the API never runs anyway, so the timing is the worker's to report.

post.summary: Push the HTTPS configuration to the edge (admin)
post.description: Renders the effective settings into a Caddyfile and loads it into the running proxy. Caddy swaps configurations atomically: a rejected one leaves the old one serving. This runs automatically on API start-up and whenever an HTTPS setting is saved, so the button is for retrying after a failure. A half-filled configuration — the switch on with a blank domain, address or token — applies the **plain HTTP** configuration rather than failing, which is the same fallback the edge's own entrypoint makes.

Asks Cloudflare two questions with the stored token: `GET /user/tokens/verify` (is it live?) and `GET /zones?name=…` for each domain's zone (can it see the zone?). A token scoped to the wrong zone passes the first and fails the second, which is exactly the mistake that would otherwise surface twenty seconds into a failed issuance. Writes nothing, issues nothing, and never logs or returns the token.

post.description: Unlike `probe`, this one **stores** what it gets: a sample row and its hourly rollup, exactly as the scheduled poller would. Useful to seed a chart without waiting for the switch, and to confirm the write path end to end.

post.summary: Backfill from the public feed page (admin)
post.description:
Fetches the feed's **public** listen page once — the login-free one any visitor gets — and backfills the hours nobody polled from the 24-hour listener sparkline it server-renders. This is the only listener *history* Broadcastify publishes anywhere: the owner API answers with one instant's count and nothing else, so without this a deployment's listener grid begins at its first poll.

The merge rule is one way round: a page value fills an hour that has no poll, and refreshes an hour a previous page fetch filled, but it **never** overwrites an hour this deployment polled — those are its own measurements. `hours_written` is therefore usually smaller than `len(bars)` once the poller has been running.

No credentials are used or needed, only `bcfy_feed_id`. This route ignores both the poller switch and the fetch interval; the scheduled fetch is unaffected. The page is undocumented HTML and may change without notice, in which case `bars` comes back empty and nothing is written.

post.summary: Import a feed dashboard CSV export (admin)
post.description:
Reads one of the two CSVs the feed-owner dashboard offers — Broadcastify → Manage → your feed → Statistics → export **hourly listeners** or **uptime** — and stores it. This is the only listener backfill that reaches further than a day: the owner API carries no history at all and the public page's sparkline carries 24 hours, while the hourly export carries about a week and the daily one about 180 days.

The format is decided by the file's header, not by a parameter. `Hour,Online Checks,Online Reports,Max Listeners` becomes hourly rows beside the polled ones; `Day,Uptime %,Max Listeners` becomes rows of a table nothing else writes. Its timestamps are **UTC** (docs/BCFY_STATS.md records how that was established).

Precedence is polled > import > page: an imported hour replaces one reconstructed from the public page, refreshes an earlier import, and never touches an hour this deployment polled — a later poll replaces it in turn. Re-importing the same file is therefore safe and idempotent.

Send it as multipart `file=@hourly_listeners.csv` or as a JSON body `{"content": "…"}`. At most 2 MB. Rows that cannot be read are counted with a reason and skipped rather than failing the import.

get.summary: The activity feed as Server-Sent Events
get.description: Tails the activity log live. Each new event is re-read from the database and sent as an `event: activity` frame with a JSON `data:` line; a comment heartbeat is sent when the feed is quiet. Admin only; authenticates with the session cookie.

Answers 200 with `status: "degraded"` rather than an error when the database is unreachable, so a monitor can tell 'the API is down' from 'the API is up and the database is not'. Includes the headline counts, the transcription queue depth, the upload flow-control gauge (`queue`), free space under `AUDIO_ROOT` and the ingest snapshot.

`disk` is the audio root's filesystem with its alert level (`ok`/`warn`/`critical`, from the `disk_*` settings) and a days-to-full estimate fitted over the worker's last 24 h of five-minute samples; `disk_volumes` lists every filesystem the worker watches.

`health` lists the health conditions the worker holds raised right now (a hot recorder silent, no new calls, transcription stalled, the database backup overdue); empty when all is well.

`counts.calls` is an estimate (`pg_class.reltuples`, within a couple of percent) refreshed at most once a minute, and `ingest` is a cached measurement that says how old it is in `as_of`/`cached_s`. Everything else is current. For a liveness probe use `/api/healthz`, which is one `SELECT 1`.

**Guests** (no session, no token) get the same shape with the operator-only fields blanked: `version` and `audio_root` are empty, `uptime_s` is 0, `database.detail` and `ingest` are null, each disk's `path` is a neutral label (`audio storage`, `storage 2`, …) and a `backup_stale` condition carries no `message`.

get.summary: Ingest lag: seconds since the newest recording
get.description: `now − max(recorded_at)` over the archive, answered from the `ix_calls_recorded_at` index — one row read, no counts and no cache. This is what the header's lag badge polls on every page; `/api/stats/overview` carries the same figure among a dozen aggregates and is meant for the Statistics page.

get.summary: Liveness: the API is up and the database answers
get.description: A single `SELECT 1` and `{"ok": true}` — nothing counted, nothing cached, no disk stat. This is what a container health check or a load balancer should poll; `/api/status` is the operator-facing picture and is far more expensive. Answers 503 when the database is unreachable, so an orchestrator can act on it.

get.summary: What the pipeline has done in the last few minutes
get.description: A live snapshot of the ingest → audio → transcription → export pipeline. Every counter is reported for the last `window` seconds **and** for the window before it, so a client can show a trend without keeping history. Also carries the queue depths, one heartbeat row per recorder instance — each with the `monitor` block the recorder reported, if it serves a live audio panel of its own, carrying `local_only` for a panel on a loopback address that only opens from that machine — and, for an administrator, the last operational log lines as a ticker. Counters are open like the rest of `/status`; `recent` is empty for anyone who is not an administrator.

The `recorder` block is what keyup wants of the *instance* — currently `spool_only`, the upload hold — on its own `version`, which the recorder echoes back as `recorder_applied.version` in its status push; a null `spool_only` means keyup has no opinion and the recorder keeps its own config/panel value. post.summary: Claim one call for upload to Broadcastify Calls
post.description: Ask before uploading: **may I** POST this call to Broadcastify Calls? Answered `granted: true` for the first claimant of a talkgroup and second (±2 s), and `granted: false` with the `holder` for everyone after — a recorder told no skips the upload and reports `broadcastifyOutcome=claim_denied` on its call push. Asking twice with the same `instance_id` is granted the same claim, so a retry is safe. This exists because two recorders hear every call and Broadcastify keys a duplicate on `(system, tg, ts)` with a **whole-second** `ts`: two uploaders that rounded the same transmission a second apart do not look like a duplicate there, they look like two calls (docs/EXPORTERS.md). keyup's own exporter claims here too, as `keyup`. The claim never waits more than about a second on another claimant of the same talkgroup: past that it answers **503** with `Retry-After`, which a recorder treats like any unanswered claim — it uploads anyway, because a duplicate Broadcastify can often catch is cheaper than a lost call. Needs the `upload` scope.

post.summary: A recorder reports what its tuners are doing
post.description: One report of every tuner's live status — serial, backend, center/span, role, lock state, control-channel health, pool usage, the hardware the operator says is on it, its front-end settings (`gain`/`gains`/`agc`, `ppm` with `auto_ppm_applied`, `bandwidth_hz`, `rx_port`, `settings`, `lna_db`/`vga_db`/`amp`, `sample_rate`, `data_follow`, `control_frequencies`), the `gain_elements` it has and the `capabilities` saying which of them change without a restart, any desired fields it `rejected`, its wideband level and frequency error, and the desired version it has applied. The body may also carry the recorder's own `station` (what and where the site is) and `counters` (instance-level lifetime totals); each of those is written only when present — omitting one leaves the stored value alone rather than clearing it, and the same goes for `uplink` (what the recorder's upload path is doing: holding or not, where that came from, what is waiting in the spool), `link` (the peers it is linked to), `event_log` (its own archive backlog) and `recorder_applied` (the recorder-level desired version it has applied). `monitor` — where the recorder serves its own live audio panel — is the one block that does **not** follow that rule: omitting it clears the stored one, because it becomes a link an operator clicks. Unknown tuner keys create rows; a malformed entry is skipped, never fatal. Bumps the recorder's last-seen and announces `tuner.status` on the live bus. Needs the `upload` scope.

Frames are never stored and never routed through the database — keyup caches only the latest per tuner and fans it out to any live viewer over `GET /admin/recorders/spectrum/stream`. A frame for a tuner keyup does not yet know (no status push has created it) is ignored. Needs the `upload` scope.

Admin only.

put.description: Writes what keyup wants one tuner to do — role, focus site, center frequency, enabled, spectrum, bands — and how its front end is set up: `gain`/`gains`/`agc`, `ppm` with `auto_ppm`/`auto_ppm_limit`, `bandwidth_hz`, `rx_port`, raw Soapy `settings`, the HackRF `lna_db`/`vga_db`/`amp`, `sample_rate`, `data_follow` and the `control_frequencies` to hunt. The given fields are merged onto whatever was there (omitted leaves it, a value sets it, an explicit null clears it). Bumps the tuner's `desired_version` and the recorder's `version`, and announces `tuner.status` on the bus. Refused with a 422 naming the field: a role outside auto|control|voice|data; a center frequency outside the reported span; a `bands` entry that is neither a known label nor an explicit `lo-hi` range in Hz; `ppm` beyond ±200; a `gains` key the tuner did not report in `gain_elements`, or a value outside that element's range; an overall `gain` outside the sum of those ranges; `lna_db` off its 8 dB step to 40 or `vga_db` off its 2 dB step to 62; a control candidate that is not a multiple of 12 500 Hz or falls outside the span; a `sample_rate` that is not an even whole number of at least four 12.5 kHz channels; and a Soapy-only field on a tuner reporting the `hackrf` backend or a HackRF-only field on one that is not. Everything is checked against what the tuner last *reported*, so a tuner that has said nothing is checked only where it can be. Admin only; creates the tuner if it does not exist.

put.summary: Set a recorder's policy and desired state (admin)
put.description:
Writes what this recorder is *for*: its `label`, its `priority` (lower is preferred when several recorders could cover one site) and its `standby` class — `hot` records whenever it is healthy, `warm` waits with its tuners disabled until the arbiter promotes it, `cold` is never touched automatically.

It also writes the recorder's own **desired state**, the three settings that are the instance's business rather than a tuner's: `spool_only` (the upload hold), `event_log_archive` (ship the daily raw event log here) and `link` (the whole recorder-to-recorder block). All three are three-valued — a value, or an explicit `null` that withdraws keyup's opinion and leaves the recorder on its own config, or the key left out of the body entirely, which changes nothing. Every write that actually changes one of them bumps `desired_recorder_version`, which the recorder echoes back once it has applied it; a write of the value already stored bumps nothing.

`link` is written as a unit and refused with a 422 naming the field: `bind` and each peer must be `host:port` (a hostname, an IPv4 address, or an IPv6 one in brackets, port 1…65535), peers must not repeat, an enabled link needs at least one peer, the shared key must be at least 16 characters and `hello_interval_s` must be 1…60. Omitting `key` from an update keeps the stored one. The key never comes back here — `desired_link` renders `key_set` and `key_fingerprint` instead.

`instance_id` renames the recorder and rewrites the instance text on everything it has already filed; a name another recorder holds is a 409. Omitted fields are left alone. This never touches a tuner's desired state: only the arbiter turns policy into tuner writes, and only by flipping `enabled`. Admin only.

delete.description: Removes a recorder and its tuners from the roster. Nothing it recorded is touched — calls carry the recorder's *name*, not a foreign key onto this row — so this forgets a machine that has been retired, not its archive. A recorder that has reported within the last hour is a 409 unless `force=true`: a live recorder is re-created by its very next poll, so deleting one only loses the label and standby policy an operator set on it. DesiredBroadcastify.title: DesiredBroadcastify
DesiredBroadcastify.description:
Everything a recorder needs to upload its own calls to Broadcastify Calls (§4.8).

Sent only while ``broadcastify_upload_at`` is ``recorder``, the Calls switch is on and
the credentials for the selected environment are present; ``null`` in every other
case, and ``null`` is the instruction — a recorder that stops being sent this block
stops uploading and keyup takes the calls back.

Like ``link`` it is all-or-nothing and, like ``link``, it is one of the two responses
that carry a credential in clear: it goes to the recorder that has to register with
it and nowhere else (:func:`public_broadcastify` is what an operator sees).

``revision`` rather than a version counter: this block is derived from runtime
*settings*, which no per-recorder generation number tracks, so the recorder compares
the hash and re-reads its credentials when it changes.  ``DesiredRecorder.version`` is
deliberately **not** bumped for it.

Sent as a unit: a peer list is meaningless without the key it authenticates with. This is the only response that carries the shared `key` in clear, and it goes only to the recorder that must hold it.

Not covered by `version`: it is derived from the talkgroup table, so the recorder compares its `revision`. An older recorder that ignores this field is not wrong, only wasteful — keyup stores the metadata and deletes the audio at once.

Carries the Calls API key in clear, like `link` above, and for the same reason. Not covered by `version`: it is derived from runtime settings, so the recorder compares its `revision`.

DesiredRecorder.title: DesiredRecorder
DesiredRecorder.description:
The desired state of the **recorder itself**, alongside its tuners' (§4.8).

Its ``version`` is deliberately not the recorder-level ``version`` beside it: that one
moves whenever any *tuner* is edited, and a counter the recorder echoes back cannot be
one an unrelated tuner write keeps shifting.  This one is bumped by an operator write of
any field in *this* block, and the recorder returns it as ``recorder_applied.version``.

**Every field here is three-valued and null is the important value**: null means keyup
has no opinion, so the recorder keeps whatever its own TOML or front panel says.  Null is
the default on all of them, which is what stops a recorder keyup has never been told
anything about from being reconfigured by silence.

``link`` is the odd one only in size: it is the whole recorder-to-recorder block or
nothing at all, because half a link — peers without the key they authenticate with — is
not a link.  It is the one place the shared ``key`` is sent in clear, and it goes only
here, to the recorder that has to hold it.

tgids.description: The tgids to drop at the recorder, ascending. Keyed by tgid alone — a recorder knows the number it decoded, not which of keyup's systems it belongs to — so a tgid is listed only when it is skippable everywhere it appears

revision.description: 12 hex characters of a sha256 over the sorted list; unchanged means nothing to do

DesiredSkipTalkgroups.title: DesiredSkipTalkgroups
DesiredSkipTalkgroups.description:
The talkgroups a recorder should not upload at all (§4.8).

A talkgroup lands here only when *every* use keyup could put its audio to has been
turned off: ``record`` is false (do not keep the recording), ``transcribe`` is false (do
not keep the words), and no export service's selection publishes it.  With all three
false the upload would be a file keyup ingests, stores, and deletes on the next discard
pass, having learned nothing from it — so the cheapest place to stop it is before it is
ever sent.

It is an **exclusion** list rather than a record list on purpose.  A recorder that
cannot reach keyup, or one running a build that does not know this field, keeps
uploading everything: the failure mode of a missing list is a full archive, never a
silent hole in one.

``null`` when the list is empty, which is what every deployment ships as.  Like
:class:`DesiredBroadcastify`, this is derived from the talkgroup table rather than from
anything stored per recorder, so it carries its own ``revision`` and
``DesiredRecorder.version`` is **not** bumped for it.

``version`` is the recorder-level generation: it changes whenever any tuner's desired

:class:`DesiredTuner` (its own ``version`` and the ``config`` to apply).  ``recorder``
carries what keyup wants of the *instance* rather than of a tuner — currently the
upload hold — with its own version to echo.

version.title: Version
version.description: This tuner's desired_version; echo it back as applied_version

config.title: Config
config.description: What to tune to: enabled, role, site, center_frequency, gains, spectrum …

DesiredTuner.title: DesiredTuner
DesiredTuner.description:
One tuner's desired state as the recorder receives it: its own version plus config.

``version`` is that tuner's ``desired_version``.  The recorder applies ``config`` and
echoes ``version`` back as ``applied_version`` in its next status push; keyup calls the
tuner *drifted* while the two differ, so the recorder must be told the per-tuner version
(a recorder-level counter alone cannot tell it which tuner changed).

path.title: Path
path.description: The directory measured — the first watched path on that filesystem

level.title: Level
level.description: `warn` under `disk_warn_free_percent` or `disk_warn_free_gb`, `critical` under the critical pair — whichever of each pair trips first

growth_bytes_per_day.title: Growth Bytes Per Day
growth_bytes_per_day.description: How fast free space is shrinking, from the last 24 h of five-minute samples

days_to_full.title: Days To Full
days_to_full.description: free_bytes ÷ growth — null when free space is not shrinking or there is under an hour of samples

DiskStatusOut.title: DiskStatusOut
DiskStatusOut.description: Free space on one filesystem the app writes to (app/disk_watch.py).

EmbedPresetOut.title: EmbedPresetOut
EmbedPresetOut.description: A built-in feed the embed's filter bar can start from: its slug and a short name.

bytes.title: Bytes
bytes.description: How many bytes were written, which is what was verified

EventLogAccepted.title: EventLogAccepted
EventLogAccepted.description: What ``POST /recorder/event-log`` answers once the day is on disk and verified.

EventLogArchiveOut.title: EventLogArchiveOut
EventLogArchiveOut.description:
One archived day of one recorder's event log, as the operator's list shows it.

Deliberately without the on-disk ``path``: it is an absolute path inside the API
container and says nothing to a browser, which fetches the file from
``GET /admin/event-logs/{archive_id}/download`` instead.

ExistsRequest.title: ExistsRequest
ExistsRequest.description: The hashes a client is about to spend an upload on.

ExportJobOut.title: ExportJobOut
ExportJobOut.description: ``POST /exports`` — an async zip of audio plus metadata for a filter.

response.title: Response
response.description: What the service answered on the last attempt, as one line — Broadcastify Calls' stage-1 reply (`0 <upload id>`, `1 SKIPPED…`, `1 REJECTED…`, `100 NO-API-KEY-SPECIFIED`) or an HTTP status line. `null` on rows written before this was recorded, and on attempts that never reached an answer

response_code.title: Response Code
response_code.description: The integer leading that line: `0`, `1` or `100`

ExportLedgerRow.title: ExportLedgerRow
ExportLedgerRow.description: One ``call_exports`` row, flattened for the Admin → Exports table.

configured.title: Configured
configured.description: Whether the credentials this client needs are present

enabled_at.title: Enabled At
enabled_at.description: The enable watermark: nothing that started before this is ever uploaded

talkgroup_mode.title: Talkgroup Mode
talkgroup_mode.description: `all` (ignore the per-talkgroup checkbox), `allow` (only ticked), `deny` (all but cleared)

systems.title: Systems
systems.description: Keyup system ids selected; empty means every system

counts_24h.title: Counts 24H
counts_24h.description: The same tallies over rows touched in the last 24 hours

duplicates.title: Duplicates
duplicates.description: All-time rows the service answered as a call it already has (`1 SKIPPED---ALREADY-RECEIVED-THIS-CALL`). Not a failure and not a decision taken here: somebody else's uploader, or an earlier run of this one, got there first

duplicates_24h.title: Duplicates 24H
duplicates_24h.description: The same, over the last 24 hours

duplicate_uploads_24h.title: Duplicate Uploads 24H
duplicate_uploads_24h.description: Rows from the last 24 hours skipped here because another copy of the same transmission had already been uploaded (two recorders, and reconciliation changed which copy is primary after the first was published). Nothing was sent. Distinct from `duplicates_24h`, which is the service telling us it already holds a call somebody else sent

late_24h.title: Late 24H
late_24h.description: Rows from the last 24 hours skipped here because the call was already past Broadcastify's skew window when its turn came — no request was sent. Broadcastify Calls only; the Feed and OpenMHz have no skew rule

responses_24h.title: Responses 24H
responses_24h.description: The last 24 hours of stored responses, counted by class: `0 OK`, `1 SKIPPED`, `1 REJECTED-CALL-SKEW-TOO-LONG`, `100 NO-API-KEY-SPECIFIED`, else the code and the first word. The per-call tail (the upload id, the skew in seconds) is stripped so the histogram has one entry per kind of answer

upload_at.title: Upload At
upload_at.description: Who POSTs the call: `keyup` (this host, after ingest) or `recorder` (each trunkd recorder, at call end, with keyup recording the outcome). `broadcastify_upload_at`; Broadcastify Calls only

by_recorder_24h.title: By Recorder 24H
by_recorder_24h.description: Uploaded rows from the last 24 hours a **recorder** sent and reported on the call push, rather than this host. The rest of `counts_24h.uploaded` is keyup's

claimed_24h.title: Claimed 24H
claimed_24h.description: Rows from the last 24 hours skipped because another uploader had claimed the call first — no request was sent. Normal while `upload_at` is `recorder`: it is keyup standing down for the recorder that got there first

queue_depth.title: Queue Depth
queue_depth.description: Pending rows waiting for this service

environment.title: Environment
environment.description: Broadcastify Calls only: `production` or `development`. Broadcastify issues the two sets of credentials separately and each endpoint refuses the other's, so this picks the URL, the API key and the system id together

status_url.title: Status Url
status_url.description: The service's own monitoring page for this environment

manage_url.title: Manage Url
manage_url.description: The node-management page, where the environment has one

clock_offset_s.title: Clock Offset S
clock_offset_s.description: How far this host's clock is from its reference, in seconds; positive means ahead. `null` when it could not be measured, which is not the same as bad. Step 1 of the Broadcastify Calls workflow requires NTP accuracy because `ts` is part of the tuple they deduplicate on

clock_ok.title: Clock Ok
clock_ok.description: `|offset| <= 2 s`. `null` when the offset could not be measured

clock_source.title: Clock Source
clock_source.description: `ntp` (an SNTP query), `http` (a response's Date header), or `null`

ExportServiceStatus.title: ExportServiceStatus
ExportServiceStatus.description: One outbound service: its switch, its configuration, and how the queue is doing.

broadcastify_feed.description: The Broadcastify **Feed** (live audio stream), which has no ledger

trunked_systems.title: Trunked Systems
trunked_systems.description: Every system Broadcastify **Calls** may publish — the trunked ones (`systems.is_trunked`). An empty list means the Calls uploader has nothing it could ever send, whatever its switch says, and the page offers the switch disabled rather than letting it be turned on against a conventional archive.

ExportStatusOut.title: ExportStatusOut
ExportStatusOut.description: ``GET /admin/exports`` — both services, plus the last few ledger rows.

overrides.title: Overrides
overrides.description: `{setting_key: value}` for keys belonging to this service. A key from another service, or one that is not a runtime setting at all, is a 422 — a test must not be a way to smuggle a value past the settings API. Secrets are accepted (that is what is being tested); an empty secret means 'use the stored one'.

ExportTestRequest.title: ExportTestRequest
ExportTestRequest.description:
Optional body of the two test endpoints: the card's **unsaved** values.

The test button is pressed while filling the form in, so testing what is *stored*
answers a question nobody asked — "is the key I have not saved yet correct" is the
whole point of pressing it. `overrides` is that draft: keys of `SETTINGS_SPEC`,
restricted to the service being tested, coerced exactly as a save would coerce them,
layered over the effective settings **for this request only** and never written.

checked.title: Checked
checked.description: What this test was actually able to verify

environment.title: Environment

clock_ok.title: Clock Ok

used_draft.title: Used Draft
used_draft.description: True when the test ran against **unsaved** values sent in the request body rather than what is stored. Nothing sent that way is ever persisted.

draft_keys.title: Draft Keys
draft_keys.description: Which setting keys the draft supplied, in the order they were applied

ExportTestResult.title: ExportTestResult
ExportTestResult.description:
``POST /admin/exports/{service}/test`` — what could be checked without publishing.

`checked` says in prose exactly what was proven; read it before reading `ok`. Nothing
is ever uploaded here. Broadcastify Calls does have a real credential check — the
documented `test=1` parameter alongside `apiKey` and `systemId` — and it registers no
call and returns no upload URL; OpenMHz has none, and its public `/{shortName}/calls`
read resolves the short name only.

source.title: Source
source.description: Who is asserting the link (`cad`, `manual`, …). Anything but `manual` makes `link_confidence` and `link_method` required.

link_confidence.title: Link Confidence
link_confidence.description: Defaulted only for `source=manual`; required for any other source.

link_method.title: Link Method
link_method.description: Defaulted only for `source=manual`; required for any other source.

ExternalLinkIn.title: ExternalLinkIn
ExternalLinkIn.description:
Body of ``POST /links``.

The defaults describe a person: ``source='manual'``, ``link_confidence='strong'``,
``link_method='manual'``.  That is right for the archive's own UI and wrong for
everything else, because an automated caller that sent only ``{call_id, external_id}``
used to be recorded as a human's confident assertion — a machine guess wearing a
librarian's signature.  So the defaults are now *only* available to the manual source:
name any other ``source`` and you must say how sure you are and how you decided, or the
request is a 422 naming the fields you left out.

ExternalLinkOut.title: ExternalLinkOut
ExternalLinkOut.description: A confirmed link to something outside this archive — a CAD incident number (§3.3).

incomplete.title: Incomplete
incomplete.description: True when at least one dimension was dropped because its query hit the facet statement timeout. The dimensions that are present are still exact for the filter; the missing ones are empty. A sidebar should say so rather than read an empty list as a zero.

FacetsOut.title: FacetsOut
FacetsOut.description: ``GET /calls/facets`` — counts per dimension for the *current* filter.

FeedIn.title: FeedIn
FeedIn.description: Create a feed: a name and a ``GET /calls`` filter object.

owner.title: Owner
owner.description: Username, when an admin is listing

FeedOut.title: FeedOut
FeedOut.description:
One feed, with the two absolute URLs a reader subscribes to.

``rss_url`` and ``atom_url`` contain the token, which **is** the credential: anybody
holding one of these URLs can read every call the filter matches.

FeedPatch.title: FeedPatch
FeedPatch.description: Edit a feed.  Every field is optional; only what is sent is changed.

FeedPresetOut.title: FeedPresetOut
FeedPresetOut.description:
A built-in feed: a fixed filter at a stable URL that holds no secret.

Unlike :class:`FeedOut` there is no token here and nothing to rotate — the URLs are
meant to be handed out, and what they publish is governed by the archive's own read
policy rather than by possession of the link.

FeedPresetTalkgroup.title: FeedPresetTalkgroup
FeedPresetTalkgroup.description:
One of the busiest channels a built-in feed covers, so a reader can see what is
actually in it rather than only how many talkgroups are filed under it.

timezone.title: Timezone
timezone.description: The clock both matrices are cut on

peak_source.title: Peak Source
peak_source.description: Which history the peak was read from, and therefore how precise `peak_at` is. `samples` is one poll and names the minute; `hourly` is an hour row (imported or page-derived included) and names the hour; `daily` is a day of the dashboard export and names only the day, reported at that day's UTC midnight. Equal counts prefer the sharper source.

listeners_hours_covered.title: Listeners Hours Covered
listeners_hours_covered.description: How many hours of the window carry a listener figure — polled hours plus any reconstructed from the public feed page. The owner API returns one instant's count and no history, so this begins at this deployment's first poll and, before that, reaches back at most the 24 hours the public page's sparkline shows. Compare it with `window_hours` before reading a long window's grid.

hours_from_page.title: Hours From Page
hours_from_page.description: How many of those hours came from the **public feed page**'s 24-hour sparkline rather than from this deployment's own polls. Those hours are real listener figures and are in every grid, but they are Broadcastify's rounded hourly numbers for hours nobody here was watching — a poll always replaces one.

hours_from_import.title: Hours From Import
hours_from_import.description: How many of those hours came from the **feed dashboard's hourly CSV export** rather than from this deployment's own polls. That export is Broadcastify's own authoritative figure for the hour and it carries about a week, so it outranks a page-derived hour and is still replaced by the first real poll that lands in it.

daily.title: Daily
daily.description: One row per **UTC day** of the window from the dashboard's daily CSV export: the day's uptime percentage and its peak listener count. About 180 days of it exist where the hourly history has about seven, so this is usually the only thing in the summary that covers a long window. Empty until an import; days the export never covered are absent rather than zero.

daily_days_covered.title: Daily Days Covered
daily_days_covered.description: How many days of the window `daily` actually carries

first_sample_at.title: First Sample At
first_sample_at.description: The first hour ever polled: where the listener history starts

history_from.title: History From
history_from.description: The earliest day this feed has **any** listener figure for — hourly or daily. After an import of the daily export this is months before `first_sample_at`, which is why they are two fields: one is where the history starts, the other is where the *hourly* history starts.

calls_hours_covered.title: Calls Hours Covered
calls_hours_covered.description: How many hours of the window contain calls this feed carries

listeners_hour_of_week.title: Listeners Hour Of Week
listeners_hour_of_week.description: 7x24, Monday first, average listeners per cell. A cell is `null` — not `0` — when no poll fell in it, so an unmeasured hour never reads as an empty one.

listeners_max_hour_of_week.title: Listeners Max Hour Of Week
listeners_max_hour_of_week.description: The same grid's highest single reading per cell; `null` where unmeasured

listeners_samples_hour_of_week.title: Listeners Samples Hour Of Week
listeners_samples_hour_of_week.description: How many polls each cell of the listener grid is built from

calls_hour_of_week.title: Calls Hour Of Week
calls_hour_of_week.description: The same grid for local call volume — the talkgroups the `export_broadcastify` selection covers, so it is the traffic this feed actually carries.

quietest_hours.title: Quietest Hours
quietest_hours.description: The ten *least* busy cells — the maintenance question. Ranked by average listeners among cells that have listener samples, tie-broken by call volume.

quietest_basis.title: Quietest Basis
quietest_basis.description: What `quietest_hours` and `quiet_windows` were computed from. `calls` means no listener sample exists yet and the ranking fell back to radio traffic, which is a weaker claim: it says the radio is quiet, not that nobody is listening.

quiet_windows.title: Quiet Windows
quiet_windows.description: The three quietest non-overlapping runs of at least two hours — long enough to restart a feed in, which the single quietest hour is not.

correlation.title: Correlation
correlation.description: Pearson's r between hourly call volume and hourly average listeners. `null` when fewer than 24 paired hours exist or either series never varies — an r over three hours would be a number with no information in it.

FeedSummary.description: ``GET /admin/bcfy-stats/summary`` — the whole Feed stats page in one object.

widened.title: Widened

HealthConditionOut.description: One health condition the worker currently holds raised (app/health.py).

HotHour.description: One cell of the hour-of-week grid, in a ranking.

HttpsStatusOut.description: Everything the HTTPS tab's status card shows.

rows_skipped.description: Rows the parser could not read

skipped_reasons.description: Why rows were skipped, counted per reason rather than listed per row — a file that is entirely the wrong thing says so in one line.

ImportReport.description: What one dashboard CSV import parsed, wrote and refused.

skipped_service_tags.title: Skipped Service Tags
skipped_service_tags.description: CSV rows whose `service_tag`/`tag` cell named no RadioReference tag. The rest of the row was imported; only the tag was dropped.

skipped_agency_codes.title: Skipped Agency Codes
skipped_agency_codes.description: CSV rows whose `agency_code` cell named no agency in this deployment (see `GET /agencies`). Dropped the same way, and for a harder reason: the column is a foreign key, so writing one would abort the whole import at that row.

ingest_lag_s.title: Ingest Lag S
ingest_lag_s.description: Seconds since the newest call was recorded; null on an empty archive

IngestLagOut.title: IngestLagOut
IngestLagOut.description: ``GET /api/status/lag`` — how stale the archive is, and nothing else.

IngestMigrationProgressIn.title: IngestMigrationProgressIn
IngestMigrationProgressIn.description:
What a bulk-import run posts about itself.

The import tool is a CLI on somebody's laptop, not part of this process, so its progress
can only be *reported*.  ``label`` names (and, the first time, creates) the ``migration``
source row it reports against — which is what turns "a long import is running somewhere"
into a card on the Ingest tab.

IngestSourceIn.description:
A place recordings come from — the body of POST/PUT ``/admin/ingest/sources``.

One model for three kinds, with the per-kind fields optional and validated by the
endpoint, rather than three models: the operator's mental object is "a source", the
three kinds differ by a handful of fields, and a discriminated union would put that
difference in the schema at the cost of three names to keep in step.

IngestSourceOut.description:
One source, with whatever is known about whether it is actually working.

``path_state`` is checked on read rather than stored, because the interesting failure —
an NFS mount that went away at 03:00 — happens long after the save that validated it.

IngestSourceStatusOut.description: What one source has actually done lately — the answer to "is this thing on".

IngestSourcesOut.title: IngestSourcesOut
IngestSourcesOut.description: Every source, plus the generation the watcher is polling for.

auth_required_read.description: False while reads are open to anonymous visitors

windows.description: Observation windows this message appeared in

exemplar.title: Exemplar
exemplar.description: Hex body, when the decoder could not name it

enabled.description: True when the recorder is serving its live monitor

url.title: Url
url.description: The panel's base URL — often a loopback address that only works on that host

token_required.title: Token Required
token_required.description: True when the panel asks for the recorder's token first

max_streams.title: Max Streams
max_streams.description: How many listeners it will serve at once

MonitorIn.title: MonitorIn
MonitorIn.description:
``monitor`` on the status push — the recorder's own live audio panel, if it serves one.

Keyup does not carry this audio.  The recorder streams what it is hearing from a small
server of its own and this block says where that is, so the status page can offer the
operator a link and nothing more.  A recorder built without the panel sends no block at
all, which is what ``enabled``/``url`` being absent has to mean here as well.

Unknown keys are **dropped** rather than kept — the opposite of ``UplinkIn``, and for a
reason: this block is read for one purpose (render a link) and is the only recorder
report whose stored content becomes an ``href`` on somebody's status page, so the column
holds the six fields keyup knows the meaning of and nothing a future recorder invents.

``url`` is very often a loopback address: the panel binds to 127.0.0.1 by default, and
that link works only in a browser running on the recorder itself.  Keyup stores it
exactly as reported and says so beside the link rather than trying to rewrite it into
something routable, which it has no way to know.

ObservationAdjacentIn.title: ObservationAdjacentIn
ObservationAdjacentIn.description: A neighbor from an Adjacent Status Broadcast.

ObservationBandIn.title: ObservationBandIn
ObservationBandIn.description: One IDEN band-plan entry, stored with the document and not normalized.

ObservationChannelIn.title: ObservationChannelIn
ObservationChannelIn.description: A control channel the site is using or announcing as a backup.

ObservationExemplarIn.title: ObservationExemplarIn
ObservationExemplarIn.description:
One vendor message the recorder counted but could not name.

25 % of every TSBK on one L3Harris control channel is one of two L3Harris messages that
never change a byte (docs/NON-VOICE-DATA.md §3.1).  Storing 23 400 identical rows an
hour would be absurd; one exemplar per window is enough to notice the day they change.

ObservationServicesIn.title: ObservationServicesIn
ObservationServicesIn.description:
The SYS_SVC_BCAST bitmap as the recorder decodes it: which services the site says it
offers and which it supports, as names and as the raw 24-bit hex, plus the request
priority.  It was sent from the first day the recorder decoded the message and dropped
here for want of a field — ``null`` in 492 windows across three sites before this.

ObservationSiteIn.description: The site, from the RFSS/Network Status broadcast.

ObservationSystemIn.title: ObservationSystemIn

ObservationTrafficIn.description: A traffic channel the site granted during the window.

RadioEventIn.title: RadioEventIn
RadioEventIn.description:
One decoded control-channel message about a radio.

Every field is optional and every field is lenient, which is deliberate and is the one
unusual thing about this model.  A recorder posts a thousand of these at a time and
cannot inspect the archive's reply per event; if pydantic refused the *batch* because
one event carried a timestamp its clock produced badly, the recorder's only recourse
would be to drop 999 good events or to retry the same bad batch for ever.  So the
validation happens in the fold instead (:mod:`app.ingest.events`), which counts what it
could not use and stores the rest — see ``rejected`` on the response.

The messages differ from each other too: a de-registration names a radio and no
talkgroup, an affiliation names both, an SNDCP grant names a frequency.  A ``kind`` the
archive does not know is stored as ``other`` with the opcode kept.

radio_id.title: Radio Id
radio_id.description: The unit number on the air

RadioPresence.title: RadioPresence

``last_seen_at`` moves for a call **or** a control-channel event; the other two move
only for a registration or a de-registration, so a radio that has never been heard on
a site the recorder watches has all three NULL.

spool_only.description: The spool_only value it applied at that version

event_log_archive.title: Event Log Archive
event_log_archive.description: The event_log_archive value it applied at that version

link.title: Link
link.description: The link block it applied — `{enabled, bind, peers[], hello_interval_s, accept_remote_grants, publish_grants, defer_to_claims, key_set, key_fingerprint}`. The key itself is never echoed; the fingerprint (first 8 hex of its sha256) is what shows two peers hold the same one.

RecorderAppliedIn.title: RecorderAppliedIn
RecorderAppliedIn.description:
The recorder echoing back the recorder-level desired state it has applied.

Exactly the tuner ``applied_version`` rule, one level up: keyup calls the recorder's
desired state *pending* while this ``version`` lags ``desired_recorder_version``, so the
operator can tell "saved" from "the recorder has taken it up".

The fields beside the version are what it applied, echoed so the page can show applied
against pending per field rather than one badge for the block.  ``extra="allow"`` and a
permissive ``link``: a newer recorder growing a field of its own must not have its whole
report refused by an older keyup, and the block is rendered, never acted on.

The echoed ``link`` deliberately carries ``key_set``/``key_fingerprint`` and **not** the
key: trunkd does not send the secret back, and a second copy of it arriving over the
status push is something keyup would rather not have to think about.

errors.title: Errors
errors.description: At most five, for the recorder's log

RecorderEventsAccepted.title: RecorderEventsAccepted
RecorderEventsAccepted.description:
What the batch did.

``stored`` counts rows written, ``duplicates`` events the archive already had (the
recorder retries spooled batches, and a retry is free), ``rejected`` events that could
not be stored at all — a missing timestamp, an unusable field.  One bad event never
costs the batch: the counts are the report.

instance.title: Instance
instance.description: Which *instance* decoded these — the recorder's `instance_id`. Stamped on every row in the batch, so a site heard by two boxes can be read one box at a time. Omitted by an older recorder, which is stored as null.

RecorderEventsIn.title: RecorderEventsIn
RecorderEventsIn.description:
A batch of radio events from one recorder watching one site.

The site is named once for the whole batch, exactly as an observation names it, so a
thousand events cost one system/site resolution.  Batches are capped at 1 000 events.

RecorderLinkKeyGenerated.title: RecorderLinkKeyGenerated
RecorderLinkKeyGenerated.description:
A freshly generated shared key, which nothing has stored yet.

Generating is deliberately *not* saving: the operator gets a key to paste into both
recorders' dialogs, and it becomes this recorder's key only when the form is saved. A
route that stored it would break the link the moment someone clicked the button and
then cancelled.

key.title: Key
key.description: The shared secret in clear, or null when none is stored

key_set.title: Key Set
key_set.description: Whether a key is stored at all

key_fingerprint.title: Key Fingerprint
key_fingerprint.description: First 8 hex of its sha256 — what the list views show

RecorderLinkKeyOut.title: RecorderLinkKeyOut
RecorderLinkKeyOut.description:
The shared link key in clear — the answer to the *one* route that returns it.

Split out from :class:`RecorderOut` rather than made a field of it precisely so that it
cannot be returned by accident: a list of recorders has no way to reach this model, and
the only handler that builds one writes an activity row as it does.

alerts.title: Alerts
alerts.description: Notifications this document raised — `channel_audit` findings plus `new_kind` / `exemplar_changed` ones from the message census

RecorderObservationAccepted.title: RecorderObservationAccepted
RecorderObservationAccepted.description: What the observation endpoint answers: what it stored and what was new.

instance.title: Instance
instance.description: Which *instance* is speaking — the recorder's `instance_id`, the same identity `/recorder/tuners/status` uses. `recorder` names the software; this names the machine, and two boxes watching one site are told apart by nothing else. Omitted by an older recorder, which is stored as null.

observed_at.title: Observed At
observed_at.description: End of the observation window, ISO-8601 UTC

window_s.title: Window S
window_s.description: Length of the window in seconds

services.description: The site's SYS_SVC_BCAST service bitmap, when decoded

configured_control.title: Configured Control
configured_control.description: Control frequencies the recorder is configured to hunt

message_mix.title: Message Mix
message_mix.description: TSBK census for the window, keyed `mfid:opcode` (or `mfid/opcode`)

unknown_exemplars.title: Unknown Exemplars
unknown_exemplars.description: One sample of each message the decoder could not name

data_channel.description: SNDCP activity in the window: grants, pages, PDU counts, channels

lsd_nonzero.title: Lsd Nonzero
lsd_nonzero.description: Low-speed-data octet pairs that were not all zero

RecorderObservationIn.title: RecorderObservationIn
RecorderObservationIn.description:
One window of what a recorder saw of one site (``POST /recorder/observations``).

Only ``recorder``, ``system`` and ``observed_at`` are required; a recorder that can
only report its control channel posts those three and ``control``.  A document without
``site.label`` is stored verbatim and not normalized — every audit row hangs off a site.

station.title: Station
station.description: The operator's description of the site, as the recorder sent it

priority.title: Priority
priority.description: Which recorder to prefer when several cover one site — **lower is preferred**. Only the arbiter reads it, as the tie-break between warm spares.

standby.title: Standby
standby.description: `hot` records whenever it is healthy; `warm` is a spare kept registered with its tuners disabled, which the arbiter may enable when every hot recorder for a site has gone stale; `cold` is never touched automatically.

promoted_at.title: Promoted At
promoted_at.description: When the arbiter enabled this recorder's tuners, and null whenever it did not — a warm recorder an operator enabled by hand is never auto-demoted.

desired_spool_only.title: Desired Spool Only
desired_spool_only.description: What keyup wants of this recorder's uploads: true hold, false upload, null no opinion (the recorder keeps its own config/panel value).

desired_recorder_version.title: Desired Recorder Version
desired_recorder_version.description: The generation of `desired_spool_only`, bumped on every write

applied_recorder_version.title: Applied Recorder Version
applied_recorder_version.description: The desired_recorder_version the recorder last echoed back, or null

uplink.title: Uplink
uplink.description: What the recorder reports about its upload path: `spool_only`, `source` (config|keyup|panel), `spooled_calls`, `spool_bytes`, `url`. Null until a recorder that knows about it reports.

spool_only_pending.title: Spool Only Pending
spool_only_pending.description: True when keyup has an opinion on this recorder's uploads that the recorder has not yet echoed back — `desired_spool_only` is not null and the applied version differs from `desired_recorder_version`. The recorder-level twin of a tuner's `drift`.

desired_event_log_archive.title: Desired Event Log Archive
desired_event_log_archive.description: What keyup wants of this recorder's event-log archive: true ship the daily log, false do not, null no opinion (the recorder keeps its own config value).

desired_link.title: Desired Link
desired_link.description: The recorder-to-recorder link block keyup manages, **with the shared key removed**: `{enabled, bind, peers[], hello_interval_s, accept_remote_grants, publish_grants, defer_to_claims, key_set, key_fingerprint}`. Null means keyup does not manage the link and the recorder keeps its configured one. The key is never in a list or detail read — `key_fingerprint` (the first 8 hex of its sha256) is what shows two peers hold the same one, and `GET /admin/recorders/{id}/link/key` is the only route that returns it.

desired_broadcastify.title: Desired Broadcastify
desired_broadcastify.description: The Broadcastify Calls block this recorder is being sent, **with the API key removed**: `{enabled, endpoint_url, system_id, encoding, talkgroups, skew_limit_s, claim, claim_url, revision, api_key_set, api_key_fingerprint}`. Null — the usual answer — means keyup uploads this recorder's calls itself. Not stored on the recorder: it is derived from the export settings, so every recorder is sent the same block and it appears and disappears with `broadcastify_upload_at`. Read-only here; the key itself leaves only by the recorder's own desired-state poll.

desired_skip_talkgroups.title: Desired Skip Talkgroups
desired_skip_talkgroups.description: The talkgroup skip list this recorder is being sent, **as a count rather than the list**: `{count, revision}`. Null — the shipped answer — means every talkgroup is uploaded. Derived from the talkgroup table, so every recorder is sent the same one; the list itself is on the Talkgroups page, which is where it is changed.

recorder_pending.title: Recorder Pending
recorder_pending.description: True when keyup has *any* recorder-level opinion the recorder has not echoed back — the whole-block twin of `spool_only_pending`, which stays scoped to the upload hold. Set when at least one of `desired_spool_only`, `desired_event_log_archive` and `desired_link` is not null and `applied_recorder_version` differs from `desired_recorder_version`.

recorder_applied.title: Recorder Applied
recorder_applied.description: The whole block the recorder echoed back — `{version, spool_only, event_log_archive, link}` — so a client can show applied against pending per field. Null on a recorder that has never echoed one. Its `link` half carries `key_set`/`key_fingerprint`, never the key.

recorder_rejected.title: Recorder Rejected
recorder_rejected.description: Recorder-level desired fields this recorder refused, keyed by field name with its reason — the instance-level twin of a tuner's `rejected`, and the only trace a refusal leaves.

recorder_capabilities.title: Recorder Capabilities
recorder_capabilities.description: What the recorder said it can change live, conventionally `{"restart_on": [...]}` — the recorder-level fields that cost a restart. Rendered as a warning; nothing is refused over it.

link.title: Link
link.description: What this recorder reports about the peers it is linked to, verbatim and opaque — conventionally `{"peers": [{"instance", "alive", "last_seen", "claims"}]}`. Null on a recorder that reports none.

event_log.title: Event Log
event_log.description: What this recorder reports about its own event-log archive — days pending, the last one shipped. Opaque; what actually arrived is `GET /admin/event-logs`.

stream.description: The recorder's push channel (`WS /api/recorder/stream`): `connected`, `since` and `client_count`. **Per worker process** — the registry is in memory, so a `false` here means the worker that answered is not holding a socket for this recorder, not that nothing anywhere is.

instance_id.title: Instance Id
instance_id.description: Rename the recorder's `instance_id` — the identity it names itself by, not the display `label`. Everything already filed under the old name (`radio_events`, `recorder_observations`, `event_log_archives`, a call's `source_instance`) is rewritten to the new one in the same transaction, so the archive follows the rename rather than splitting in two. A name another recorder already holds is a 409. **The recorder itself must be reconfigured to match**: one that keeps posting the old name simply re-creates a row under it.

label.title: Label
label.description: A human name for the recorder, when its instance_id is not one

priority.title: Priority
priority.description: Lower is preferred; the arbiter picks the lowest-numbered healthy warm spare

standby.title: Standby
standby.description: hot | warm | cold — what this recorder is for

spool_only.title: Spool Only
spool_only.description: Hold this recorder's uploads in its local spool (`true`), push them (`false`), or say nothing and leave it on its own config/panel value (`null`). Unlike every other field here, an explicit `null` is a *write* — it clears keyup's opinion — while omitting the key leaves the current one alone. Every change bumps `desired_recorder_version`, which the recorder echoes back.

event_log_archive.title: Event Log Archive
event_log_archive.description: Ship the daily raw event log to keyup (`true`), do not (`false`), or say nothing and leave the recorder on its own config value (`null`). The same three-way rule as `spool_only`: an explicit `null` is a write, omitting the key is not.

link.title: Link
link.description: The whole recorder-to-recorder link block to manage — `{enabled, bind, peers[], key, hello_interval_s, accept_remote_grants, publish_grants, defer_to_claims}` — or an explicit `null` to stop managing it, which leaves the recorder on its configured link. Written as a unit, never merged: a peer list saved without the key it authenticates with is not a link. `key` is the one field that may be **omitted** on an update, which keeps the key already stored — the edit dialog does not hold the secret unless the operator revealed it. Refused with a 422 naming the field for a `bind` or peer that is not `host:port` (a hostname, an IPv4 address, or an IPv6 one in brackets, with a port of 1…65535), a duplicated peer, an enabled link with no peers, a key under 16 characters, or a `hello_interval_s` outside 1…60.

RecorderPolicyIn.title: RecorderPolicyIn
RecorderPolicyIn.description:
``PUT /admin/recorders/{id}`` — the operator's policy for one recorder.

Every field is optional and an omitted one is left alone, exactly as the tuner PUT
merges.  This is deliberately *not* where a tuner's desired state is written: policy is
what keyup should do about a recorder, ``desired`` is what the recorder should do about
a tuner, and the arbiter is the only thing that turns the first into the second.

The three **desired-state** fields — ``spool_only``, ``event_log_archive`` and ``link``
— are the exception to "null means unset": there, null is a value in its own right —
*keyup has no opinion, leave the recorder on its own setting* — so the three states are
sent as a value / ``null`` / not sent at all, and "do not touch it" is the last one.
Every write that actually changes one of them bumps ``desired_recorder_version``, which
the recorder echoes back; a write of the value already stored bumps nothing, so a form
that resubmits itself does not leave the recorder pending for ever.

``instance_id`` is the odd field out and is documented on itself: it is not policy but
the recorder's *identity*, and renaming it rewrites the instance text on everything the
recorder has already filed.

connected.title: Connected
connected.description: True when at least one push socket for this recorder is open here

since.title: Since
since.description: When the oldest of those sockets connected, or null

client_count.title: Client Count
client_count.description: How many push sockets this worker holds for the recorder

RecorderStreamOut.title: RecorderStreamOut
RecorderStreamOut.description:
Whether this recorder is holding the push channel open (``WS /recorder/stream``).

**Per worker process.**  The registry behind it lives in memory, so with several uvicorn
workers this reports the connections the worker that answered the request happens to
hold — ``connected: false`` means "not to me", not "nowhere".

query.title: Query
query.description: Query string that recreates the search

total.title: Total
total.description: Calls matching `q` and the filters, ignoring pagination

total_capped.title: Total Capped
total_capped.description: True when `total` stopped at the counting cap (50 000) and the real number is larger, as on `GET /calls`

fuzzy.description: Present only when spelling variants were looked up: with `fuzzy=true`, or when `fallback=true` found nothing exact. Absent on every exact search.

ServiceTagTerm.title: ServiceTagTerm
ServiceTagTerm.description: A RadioReference service tag, in RR's own spelling, and the category it maps to.

value.title: Value
value.description: The value in force. Always empty for a `secret`, which is stored but never read back — `is_default` is how you tell whether one is set.

kind.title: Kind
kind.description: How to render and coerce the value. `secret` is write-only: send a new value to replace it, an empty string to clear it, and leave the key out to keep it.

is_default.title: Is Default
is_default.description: True while the value still comes from the environment

SettingDefinition.title: SettingDefinition
SettingDefinition.description: One row of ``GET /admin/settings``: the env default, plus any database override.

export_broadcastify.title: Export Broadcastify
export_broadcastify.description: Whether *conventional* calls heard on this frequency — calls with no talkgroup — may be published to Broadcastify Calls. Read only when `export_broadcastify_talkgroup_mode` is `allow` or `deny`; ignored in `all`.

SiteFrequencyOut.title: SiteFrequencyOut
SiteFrequencyOut.description:
One catalogued frequency at one site, as one source describes it.

A site has a row per ``(frequency, source)`` — what the air said, what RadioReference
documents, what the recorder is configured to hunt — so the same frequency can appear
more than once with different roles.

SiteFrequencyPatch.title: SiteFrequencyPatch
SiteFrequencyPatch.description:
Body of ``PATCH /site-frequencies/{id}`` — only the export checkboxes are editable.

Everything else on the row is *observed*: the frequency, its role and its counters are
what the air, RadioReference or the recorder config said, and editing them by hand would
only make the channel audit lie.

source.description: The id and name of the site that was deleted

moved.title: Moved
moved.description: Rows repointed onto the target, as `{table: rows}`

exemplar.title: Exemplar
exemplar.description: Newest hex body, when it cannot be decoded

known.title: Known
known.description: The operator (or the registry) has named it

alerted_at.title: Alerted At
alerted_at.description: When this kind last raised an alert; one per 24 h

SiteMessageKindOut.title: SiteMessageKindOut
SiteMessageKindOut.description:
One row of ``GET /api/sites/{id}/message-kinds``.

The census (``/message-mix``) is a rolling window; this is the archive's *memory* of
what a site has ever transmitted, which is what makes a first sighting an event.

known.title: Known
known.description: True once it is named and no longer news

instance.title: Instance
instance.description: The recorder instance this was narrowed to, when one was named

SiteMessageMix.title: SiteMessageMix
SiteMessageMix.description:
``GET /api/sites/{id}/message-mix`` — the control channel's message census.

Aggregated out of ``recorder_observations.payload`` rather than a table of its own:
the histogram is the thing worth keeping, and it already arrives with every window.

SiteOccupancy.title: SiteOccupancy
SiteOccupancy.description: ``GET /admin/occupancy`` — one site's band strip, folded from its latest observation.

system_name.title: System Name
system_name.description: Name of the owning system. A site name alone is ambiguous across systems.

notes.title: Notes
notes.description: The operator's own note about this site

nac.title: Nac
nac.description: Network access code the site keys (§3.5)

rfss.title: Rfss
rfss.description: P25 RF subsystem the site belongs to

rr_synced_at.title: Rr Synced At
rr_synced_at.description: Last successful RadioReference sync of this site

services_available.title: Services Available
services_available.description: The services this site's SYS_SVC_BCAST says it is offering, from the newest observation window that carried the bitmap. **Null** means nobody has decoded the message here — which is not the same as a site offering nothing. `GET /sites/{id}/profile` has the rest of the bitmap.

deletable.title: Deletable
deletable.description: True when `DELETE /sites/{id}` would succeed — nothing references this site. The UI enables its delete button from this rather than guessing.

blocking.title: Blocking
blocking.description: What still references this site, as `{table: rows}`; empty exactly when `deletable` is true. It is what a 409 from the delete would say.

SiteOut.title: SiteOut
SiteOut.description:
A tower site of a system, e.g. ``Central``.

``name`` is unique only *within* a system: two systems can both have an ``Eastside``, and
real archives have exactly that.  ``system_name`` is carried on every row so a client never
has to render a site name on its own — "Example System / Eastside" is the only label that
identifies a site, and the SPA shows the system beside or under the name everywhere.

rr_site_id.title: Rr Site Id
rr_site_id.description: RadioReference site id, or null to unmap

SitePatch.title: SitePatch

How much of what this control channel says has ever been named.

hundreds of them — so the interesting number is ``unknown - noise``, the kinds that

One recorder instance's most recent window on this site.

Two boxes watching one tower are told apart by nothing but ``instance`` (§3.5), and the
profile below is merged across them — so this list is how a reader sees *who* saw what,
and how stale the newest sighting from each box is.

observed_by.title: Observed By

SiteProfileOut.title: SiteProfileOut
SiteProfileOut.description:
Everything Keyup knows about one tower site, in one document.

*latest stored observation per recorder instance*, newest instance winning field by
field — so a box that has been down for a day still contributes the band plan it saw,
and the live box's control channel is the one shown.

``unknowns`` is the point of the document as much as the rest of it: a site is a pile of
numbers some of which were never decoded, and a panel that only renders what is known
quietly hides how much is not (docs/UNKNOWN-DATA-PLAN.md).

elevation_m.title: Elevation M
elevation_m.description: Ground elevation above sea level, meters; the mast height is per tuner

StationIn.title: StationIn
StationIn.description:
Where and what the recorder *is*, as its operator described it.

Facts nobody but the person who built the station knows: what it is called, where it
stands, how to reach whoever runs it.  keyup stores them verbatim and never overrides
them — the recorder is the authority here, not the archive.  Every field is optional
because a station that has filled in only a name is a perfectly ordinary station.

Coordinates are WGS84 decimal degrees and are range-checked rather than clamped: a
longitude of −1810 clamped to −180 would put the station in the Pacific and say nothing
about it, while a refused push tells the operator the config is wrong.

unit_calls_24h.title: Unit Calls 24H
unit_calls_24h.description: Unit-to-unit (private) calls in the last 24 hours — a subset of `calls_24h`, not a second total to add to it.

transcript_coverage.title: Transcript Coverage

stt_rtf.title: Stt Rtf
stt_rtf.description: Audio seconds per second of processing, from transcripts

audio_discarded_24h.title: Audio Discarded 24H
audio_discarded_24h.description: Calls ingested in the last 24 hours whose audio was deleted by the discard pass because their talkgroup's **Record** toggle is off. The metadata and any transcript are still there; only the recording is gone.

no_speech_24h.title: No Speech 24H
no_speech_24h.description: Calls in the last 24 hours the audio pass found nothing in — a mic keyed and released with nothing said (`audio_meta.content = "none"`). A pager tone-out with no words behind it is `"page"` and is not one of these. They are counted in `calls_24h` like any other transmission; they are simply never transcribed or exported, and their audio is discarded when `audio_discard_no_speech` is on.

static_24h.title: Static 24H
static_24h.description: Calls in the last 24 hours that were broadband static rather than speech — a squelch tail or a failed decode, noise across the whole vocoder band (`audio_meta.content = "static"`). Refused by the same gates as `no_speech_24h` — never transcribed, never exported, and discarded when `audio_discard_no_speech` is on — and counted apart from it because a rising static count is an RF or subscriber-radio fault, not quiet traffic.

StatsOverview.title: StatsOverview
StatsOverview.description: The headline numbers on the dashboard.

SttBackendConfigIn.title: SttBackendConfigIn
SttBackendConfigIn.description:
A backend as the operator defines it — the body of POST and PUT ``/admin/stt/backends``.

Mirrors :class:`app.config.SttBackend` field for field, because the table *is* that
model with a primary key; anything else would be a second vocabulary for one concept.

``api_key`` is write-only, and its two falsy values mean different things on a PUT:
``null`` (or an omitted field) leaves the stored key alone, and ``""`` clears it.  There
is no way to read one back, so an operator editing a backend's URL must not have to
re-paste its key, and a browser must not be able to ask for it.

SttBackendDeleteOut.title: SttBackendDeleteOut
SttBackendDeleteOut.description: What a delete did — which is not always a delete.

SttBackendEnabledIn.title: SttBackendEnabledIn

SttBackendProbeOut.description:
The result of asking one backend, right now, whether it works.

Two questions in one answer: the health check (does the server respond, does it have the
model) and — when a short clip could be found in the archive — one real transcription,
because "answers its health endpoint" and "can transcribe" are not the same claim and it
is the second one the operator is about to depend on.

SttBackendPut.title: SttBackendPut
SttBackendPut.description: PUT's body: the same fields, with the name coming from the path instead.

One backend as the worker last reported it (``stt_backend_stats``).

``stale`` is the honest answer to "is anybody publishing this": the row is kept when the
worker stops so the page can say *since when*, rather than showing an empty table that
looks like an idle system.

SttBackendsOut.title: SttBackendsOut
SttBackendsOut.description: The admin backends page in one response.

SttQueueOut.title: SttQueueOut
SttQueueOut.description:
The transcription queue from ``transcription_jobs`` — the cross-process truth.

The per-backend counters are one process' memory; these numbers are what the database
says, which is what makes them comparable with what the operator sees on the Calls page.
