TunerCapabilitiesIn.title: TunerCapabilitiesIn
TunerCapabilitiesIn.description:
What the tuner can change *without restarting*, and what costs a restart.

``restart_on`` names the desired fields whose change tears the stream down and builds it
again — a gap in the recording, on a live site.  keyup never refuses one; it says so next
to the field, because an operator who knows is choosing and an operator who does not is
surprised.

TunerDescriptionIn.title: TunerDescriptionIn
TunerDescriptionIn.description:
One tuner's operator-entered hardware description: what is actually on the mast.

keyup cannot derive any of this — a receiver model, an antenna, the run of coax, a
preamp, the height it is at — so the recorder carries it through from its own config and
keyup only displays it.  It is what makes an RSSI figure mean something.

site_id.title: Site Id
site_id.description: A keyup site id to focus on

site.title: Site
site.description: A free-form site label, when there is no id

spectrum.title: Spectrum
spectrum.description: Whether to stream a spectrum for this tuner

bands.title: Bands
bands.description: Which downlink ranges this tuner may record, as band labels (`vhf`|`uhf`|`700`|`800`|`900`, case-insensitive) or explicit `"lo-hi"` ranges in Hz such as `"856000000-866000000"`; at most 16 entries of at most 64 characters, deduplicated and stored lowercase. An **empty list** clears the restriction — the tuner records anything inside its capture span. An explicit **null** removes the key from the desired state entirely, exactly as it does for every other field here, which leaves the recorder on whatever its own configuration says. The recorder refuses (and stays pending on) a list that does not overlap the span it is capturing, so a list is worth checking against the tuner's reported center and span before sending it.

gain.title: Gain
gain.description: Overall gain in dB (Soapy devices). Refused when the tuner reports a `hackrf` backend, which has no single overall gain — set `lna_db`/`vga_db` instead.

gains.title: Gains
gains.description: Per-element gain in dB, keyed by the element name the tuner reports in `gain_elements` (`LNA`, `MIX`, `IF`…). Every key must be one the tuner named and every value must fall inside that element's reported `[min, max]`.

auto_ppm.title: Auto Ppm
auto_ppm.description: Let the recorder track the control channel's frequency error and correct itself. What it has actually applied comes back as reported `auto_ppm_applied`.

auto_ppm_limit.title: Auto Ppm Limit
auto_ppm_limit.description: How far auto-ppm may wander from 0, in ppm (0…200)

bandwidth_hz.title: Bandwidth Hz
bandwidth_hz.description: Analog front-end filter bandwidth in Hz; 0 lets the driver choose

rx_port.title: Rx Port
rx_port.description: Which antenna port to receive on (Soapy devices): `RX`, `LNAW`, `TX/RX`…

settings.title: Settings
settings.description: Raw driver key/value settings passed straight to Soapy (at most 64 entries). Soapy devices only.

lna_db.title: Lna Db
lna_db.description: HackRF front-end LNA gain: 0…40 dB in 8 dB steps. HackRF only.

vga_db.title: Vga Db
vga_db.description: HackRF baseband VGA gain: 0…62 dB in 2 dB steps. HackRF only.

amp.title: Amp
amp.description: HackRF front-end amplifier on. HackRF only.

data_follow.title: Data Follow
data_follow.description: Follow SNDCP data grants as well as voice grants. Needed for the unknown-data analysis; it costs a recorder slot per data call.

remote_grants.title: Remote Grants
remote_grants.description: Let this tuner act on grants a **linked peer** published, not only the ones it decoded itself. Needs the recorder's `link` to be up and accepting them; a tuner told this on a recorder with no link comes back `rejected`. Three-valued like every other field here: null hands it back to the recorder's own config.

control_frequencies.title: Control Frequencies
control_frequencies.description: Control-channel candidates in Hz for this tuner to hunt, tried in order. Each must be a multiple of 12500 Hz and, when the tuner has reported a span, fall inside it.

sample_rate.title: Sample Rate
sample_rate.description: Capture sample rate in Hz. `sample_rate / 12500` must be an even whole number of at least 4 channels — so 50000 Hz is the floor and every step above it is 25000 Hz.

TunerDesiredIn.title: TunerDesiredIn
TunerDesiredIn.description:
``PUT /admin/recorders/{id}/tuners/{key}`` — the desired state to write for one tuner.

Every field is optional and the write is a merge: a field **omitted** from the body is
left as it was, a field sent with a **value** is set, and a field sent as **null** is
*cleared* (removed from the tuner's desired config).  So "focus no particular site" is
``{"site_id": null}``, while leaving ``site_id`` out keeps the current focus.

``center_frequency`` is validated against the tuner's last *reported* span: a retune is
limited to within half a span either side of the reported center (``center_hz ±
span_hz/2``), because the recorder cannot tune outside the window it is currently on.

``bands`` follows the same three-way rule, and its three states are worth spelling out
because two of them look alike: ``[]`` is *set to no restriction*, and ``null`` is
*stop saying anything*, which leaves the recorder on its own configured bands.

TunerGainElementIn.title: TunerGainElementIn
TunerGainElementIn.description:
One named gain stage the tuner has, and the range it accepts.

A Soapy device describes its front end as a list of these (``LNA``, ``MIX``, ``IF``…),
and the list is what makes an editable gain form possible at all: without it keyup would
be offering a slider whose ends it had guessed.  Every desired ``gains`` key is checked
against this list and every value against this element's ``[min, max]``, so a tuner that
has not reported its elements yet simply cannot have per-element gain written.

TunerGainIn.title: TunerGainIn
TunerGainIn.description:
The gain settings a tuner is actually running.

These are the frame ``rssi_dbfs`` has to be read against: the level is ADC-referenced,
so it moves with every one of these and is not a dBm figure.  Which fields are present
depends on the backend — ``gain`` for a generic Soapy device, ``lna_db``/``vga_db``/
``amp`` for a HackRF.

drift.title: Drift
drift.description: True when the recorder has not applied the current desired_version: the tuner has been edited (desired_version > 0) and reports an applied_version that differs. A tuner never edited, or one whose recorder has not reported an applied_version yet, does not count as drifted.

rejected.title: Rejected
rejected.description: Desired fields this tuner's recorder **refused**, keyed by field name with its reason, lifted out of `reported` so a client need not dig for it. A refusal does *not* hold the tuner pending: the recorder acknowledges the version either way, so `drift` clears and this is what is left to say the setting did not take.

TunerStatusEntry.title: TunerStatusEntry
TunerStatusEntry.description:
One tuner's reported status inside ``POST /recorder/tuners/status``.

Only ``tuner_key`` is required; every other field is what the recorder happens to know.
Unknown fields are accepted and stored — the reported set evolves with the recorder.

``bands`` is capped in size and in entry length like every other reported string, but
deliberately *not* run through :func:`normalize_bands`.  This is the recorder telling
keyup what it applied, and a Pydantic failure here fails the whole push — every tuner in
it — rather than one entry.  A band list a recorder read out of its own TOML is its
business to state and keyup's only to display; refusing to hear it would cost the
operator the whole status report to make a point about spelling.

station.description: The operator's description of the site. Omitting it means 'no change' — keyup keeps whatever was last reported rather than clearing it.

counters.description: Instance-level lifetime counters. Omitting it means 'no change', exactly as for `station`.

uplink.description: The recorder's upload path: whether it is holding calls in its spool, where that setting came from, and how much is waiting. Omitting it means 'no change' — an older recorder sends none and keeps whatever was last reported.

recorder_applied.description: The recorder-level desired version this recorder has applied. Omitted by a recorder that does not know about recorder-level desired state at all.

link.title: Link
link.description: What this recorder knows about the peers it is linked to — conventionally `{"peers": [{"instance", "alive", "last_seen", "claims"}]}`. Stored **verbatim and opaque**: keyup renders it and decides nothing from it, so the shape is the recorder's to grow. Omitting it means 'no change'.

event_log.title: Event Log
event_log.description: What the recorder says about its own event-log archive: whether it is `archive`-ing at all, the `source` of that setting (`config` when its own TOML decided, `keyup` when this desired state did), how many days are `pending`, the `last_archived` day and the `last_error` if the last attempt failed. Opaque like `link`; the authoritative record of what actually arrived is `GET /admin/event-logs`. Omitting it means 'no change'.

monitor.description: Where the recorder serves its own live audio monitor, if it serves one: `{enabled, url, stream_url, token_required, streams, max_streams}`. Unlike every other block here, **omitting it clears the stored one**: the value becomes a link on the status page, and a link to a panel the recorder has stopped serving is worse than no link. A recorder with no panel sends nothing and gets none.

rejected.title: Rejected
rejected.description: Recorder-level desired fields this recorder **refused**, keyed by field name with the reason — the instance-level twin of a tuner's `rejected`. A refusal does not hold the recorder pending: it acknowledges the version either way, so this map is the only trace one leaves. Omitting it means 'no change'; send `{}` to say the last apply refused nothing.

capabilities.title: Capabilities
capabilities.description: What the recorder can and cannot do live, conventionally `{"recorder": {"restart_on": ["link"]}}` — which recorder-level fields cost a restart of the process to change. Opaque and stored verbatim; keyup renders it as a warning beside those fields and refuses nothing over it. Omitting it means 'no change'.

UplinkIn.title: UplinkIn
UplinkIn.description:
What the recorder says about its **upload path**, inside the status push.

The other half of the hold: keyup says what it wants in ``desired-state.recorder`` and
the recorder answers here with what it is actually doing, where that came from — its own
``config``, this ``keyup``, or the operator's front ``panel`` — and how much is waiting
in the spool while it holds.  Every field is optional and unknown ones are kept: an
older recorder omits the whole block, and a newer one may grow it.

``source`` is not an enum on the wire.  A value keyup does not recognize is worth
storing and showing verbatim — the recorder is the authority on why it is holding — and
refusing the push over a word would cost the operator the whole report.
